The enshrined deity is Ame-no-Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto, and the shrine crest is the crossed-arrow motif. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former shrine rank was {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}. {{nihongo|'''Oi Shrine'''|意非神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Inaba Province]].

== Overview ==
This shrine was established by descendants of Ame-no-Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto to enshrine their ancestral deity. It is an ancient shrine with over a thousand years of history, listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 It stands on a hill at the entrance to the Yadora district, beyond the {{ill|Hatto river|ja|八東川|qid=Q11391449}} from {{ill|Wakasa-juku|ja|若桜宿|qid=Q11616547}}.

In ancient times it was called “'''Oi-no-miya'''” and was located in Ichinomiya Valley (Fukada), but according to tradition it was relocated to Yaotoshi Valley (= Yadora = Yadora), the place where an arrow shot from the shrine grounds by {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|de|Takenouchi no Sukune|es|Takenouchi no Sukune|fa|تاکنوشی نو سوکون|fr|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰|ko|다케우치노 스쿠네|mni|ꯇꯀꯦꯅꯣꯎꯆꯤ ꯅꯣ ꯁꯨꯀꯨꯅꯦ|pt|Takenouchi no Sukune|zh|武內宿禰|qid=Q1073668}} is said to have landed. At the foot of the hill stands Japan’s largest {{ill|Nobori|ca|Nobori|es|Nobori|fa|نوبوری|fr|Nobori|id|Nobori|ja|幟|ko|노보리|nl|Nobori|pt|Nobori|zh|幟 (日本)|qid=Q1068772}}.

== Shrine grounds ==
; Japan’s largest nobori banner
It was erected on October 8 of the first year of the Heisei era as a reconstruction of Oi Shrine’s “five-tan nobori,” which existed until around {{ill|1945|ab|1945|af|1945|als|1945|am|1945 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1945|ar|1945|ary|1945|arz|1945|ast|1945|av|1945|avk|1945|ay|1945|az|1945|azb|۱۹۴۵ (میلادی)|ba|1945 йыл|ban|1945|bar|1945|bat_smg|1945|bcl|1945|be|1945|be_x_old|1945|bg|1945|bh|1945|bjn|1945|bn|১৯৪৫|bpy|মারি ১৯৪৫|br|1945|bs|1945.|ca|1945|cdo|1945 nièng|ce|1945 шо|ceb|1945|ckb|١٩٤٥|co|1945|crh|1945|cs|1945|csb|1945|cv|1945|cy|1945|da|1945|de|1945|diq|1945|dsb|1945|el|1945|eml|1945|eo|1945|es|1945|et|1945|eu|1945|ext|1945|fa|۱۹۴۵|fi|1945|fiu_vro|1945|fo|1945|fr|1945|frp|1945|frr|1945|fur|1945|fy|1945|ga|1945|gag|1945|gan|1945年|gcr|1945|gd|1945|gl|1945|gn|1945|gor|1945|gv|1945|hak|1945-ngièn|he|1945|hi|१९४५|hif|1945|hr|1945.|hsb|1945|ht|1945 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1945|hy|1945|hyw|1945 թուական|ia|1945|id|1945|ilo|1945|inh|1945 шу|io|1945|is|1945|it|1945|ja|1945年|jbo|1945moi|jv|1945|ka|1945|kaa|1945|kbp|1945|kk|1945 жыл|kn|೧೯೪೫|ko|1945년|krc|1945 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1945|ku|1945|kv|1945-ӧд во|kw|1945|ky|1945-жыл|la|1945|lb|1945|lez|1945 йис|li|1945|lij|1945|lmo|1945|ln|1945|lt|1945 m.|ltg|1945|lv|1945. gads|mai|१९४५|map_bms|1945|mdf|1945|mg|1945|mhr|1945|mi|1945|min|1945|mk|1945|ml|1945|mn|1945 он|mnw|၁၉၄၅|mr|इ.स. १९४५|mrj|1945 и|ms|1945|my|၁၉၄၅|myv|1945 ие|mzn|۱۹۴۵|nah|1945|nap|1945|nds|1945|nds_nl|1945|new|ई सं १९४५|nl|1945|nn|1945|no|1945|nrm|1945|nso|1945|oc|1945|olo|1945|or|୧୯୪୫|os|1945-æм аз|pa|1945|pam|1945|pap|1945|pl|1945|pnb|1945|pt|1945|qu|1945|ro|1945|roa_tara|1945|ru|1945 год|rue|1945|sah|1945 сыл|sc|1945|sco|1945|sd|1945ع|se|1945|sh|1945.|shn|1945|si|1945|simple|1945|sk|1945|sl|1945|smn|1945|sq|1945|sr|1945|stq|1945|su|1945|sv|1945|sw|1945|szl|1945|ta|1945|te|1945|tet|1945|tg|Соли 1945|th|พ.ศ. 2488|tk|1945|tl|1945|tly|1945|tpi|1945|tr|1945|tt|1945 ел|ty|1945|udm|1945 ар|ug|1945 - يىلى|uk|1945|ur|1945ء|uz|1945|vec|1945|vi|1945|vls|1945|vo|1945|wa|1945|war|1945|xmf|1945|yi|1945|za|1945 nienz|zea|1945|zh|1945年|zh_classical|一九四五年|zh_min_nan|1945 nî|zh_yue|1945年|qid=Q5240}} (Shōwa 20).
A Yadora-grown {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=cedar}} (100 years old, 31 m tall) is used as the pole. The banner measures 26.8 m in height and 1.8 m in width, equivalent in area to 30 tatami mats.
The calligraphy was done by {{ill|Shigenobu Sakano|ja|坂野重信|qid=Q11425611}} for the banner, {{ill|Yūji Nishio|ja|西尾邑次|vi|Nishio Yūji|qid=Q11627787}} for the hoisting platform, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kenji Takemoto}} for the commemorative monument.

; One of Japan’s largest wooden torii gates
Erected on January 30 of Heisei 23 to commemorate the 20th anniversary of the accession of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Emperor Akihito}}.
As with the banner pole, it was built using Yadora-grown {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=cedar}} (over 80 years old, milled from trees 18 m tall).
Its dimensions are 10.8 m in height and 9.2 m in width, ranking it among the top five wooden torii gates in Japan (as of May, Heisei 23).
The shrine name plaque calligraphy was done by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Norie Nagano}}, head of the Tottori Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines. The initiator and overall person in charge was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Masayuki Iino}}, head parish representative of Oi Shrine.
